title: Gravitas: an interactive astrophysics sandbox for teaching
description:
Gravitas is a browser-based N-body gravity sandbox and astronomy teaching tool. It ships 59 configurable scenarios drawn from real and idealized systems, 23 guided investigations in which undergraduate students predict, measure and plot their own data, instructor materials with answer keys, and a public account of what the underlying model does and does not represent.

Alongside the investigations are 3 classroom activities — shorter formats built from the same lesson steps, from a five-minute demonstration to a full lab — and 54 generated instructor documents: a guide and an answer key for every investigation, activity guides and student worksheets, an adopter’s guide and a curriculum map. Answer keys are derived from the lesson definitions and verified against the same function that marks student work, so they cannot disagree with what a student sees.

It runs entirely client-side as a static site, requires no account or installation, and encodes any simulation state into a shareable URL. It works offline after a first visit, targets WCAG 2.2 Level AA with axe-core run over 15 surfaces in 2 languages and 2 themes on every build, and is published in English and Spanish.

The physics is checked in public: 243 checks of the engine against analytic results, published values and independent integrations, each with its measured error and the kind of evidence it rests on, at gravitas-sim.online/validation/. A companion page states what the model represents and, at equal length, what it does not.

Live at gravitas-sim.online.
